title: Roman image-cult is rightly called adoratio; praxis is prostration, kneeling, uncovering, kiss, candles, incense
source_text: II. Manifestum quoque fecimus cultum quem Ecclesia Romana imaginibus defert, juxta communem scholae ipsius usum, imo & conciliorum quibus se subjicit definitiones, adorationis voce recte exprimi; adeoque cultum illum, ex conciliorum eorundem doctrina, & Romanae Ecclesiae praxi, imaginibus rite & pie exhiberi, coram iis procumbendo, genua flectendo, & caput aperiendo, itemque eas osculando, & offerendo cereos & incensum.
pass_a_gloss: We have also made manifest that the cult which the Roman Church pays to images, according to the common usage of her own school, and indeed the definitions of the councils to which she subjects herself, is rightly expressed by the word adoration; and accordingly that that cult, from the doctrine of those same councils, and from the praxis of the Roman Church, is duly and piously exhibited to images, by prostrating before them, bending the knee, and uncovering the head, and likewise by kissing them, and by offering candles and incense.
pass_b_english: School and Councils name the image-cult adoratio without embarrassment.
The living praxis is bodily: prostration, genuflection, bare head, kiss, candles, and incense.

choices.why: Lived Roman usage, not mere theory.
